title: B2B software rep
tagline: Learn to justify software spend to skeptical finance leaders who protect every dollar.
you_are: an enterprise account executive selling a B2B SaaS platform
setting: Conversations happen over video calls, in glass-walled conference rooms, and at quiet coffee bars near the prospect’s office.

scenarios.label: First discovery call
scenarios.desc: A 30-minute video call to uncover pain points and qualify the opportunity.
scenarios.setup: You join a scheduled Zoom. The CFO appears on screen, notebook open, and says: Thanks for the deck, I’ve skimmed it. You have ten minutes to show me why this isn’t just another tool we don’t need.
scenarios.skills: Discovery questioning, business case framing, time management
scenarios.objective: Secure a committed next step with a defined decision timeline.
scenarios.moment: Tuesday 10:15 am, bright morning light through blinds

scenarios.label: ROI workshop with finance team
scenarios.desc: A working session where the CFO brings their controller and FP&A lead to stress-test your model.
scenarios.setup: You sit at the head of a glass-walled conference room. The CFO taps a printed spreadsheet and says: Your assumptions on churn reduction are aggressive. Walk us through the math without the marketing fluff.
scenarios.skills: Financial modeling, objection handling, stakeholder alignment
scenarios.objective: Get the finance team to sign off on a mutual business case they can defend internally.
scenarios.moment: Thursday 2:00 pm, overcast sky muting reflections on glass

scenarios.label: Renewal negotiation at scale
scenarios.desc: A high-stakes renewal where the CFO threatens to cut seats or switch vendors unless price drops.
scenarios.setup: You meet at a quiet cafe corner table. The CFO slides a competitor’s one-pager across the surface and says: They’re forty percent cheaper at three-year term. Convince me to stay before I sign Monday.
scenarios.skills: Value reinforcement, competitive positioning, concession strategy
scenarios.objective: Retain the account at acceptable terms without eroding baseline ARR.
scenarios.moment: Friday 4:30 pm, golden hour through tall windows

buyers.angle: She will end the call early if the first five minutes lack a crisp hypothesis on her specific margin pressure.
He treats every software pitch as a CapEx trap and demands on-premise equivalency proof.

buyers.role: CFO with FP&A director and controller
buyers.angle: She lets her team dismantle your model cell by cell; you must defend every input variable.
He has a signed term sheet from a competitor and uses it to compress your pricing to marginal cost.
She only cares about payback within the current fund cycle and discounts strategic value to zero.

objections: Show me the net new ARR this creates, not efficiency fluff
Your implementation timeline assumes zero adoption friction; redo it
We’re not funding a science project; where is the hard dollar savings line item?
The competitor includes implementation in that price; yours is extra
Our audit committee will not approve a vendor without SOC 2 Type 2
If churn ticks up one percent your ROI goes negative; that’s not a buffer
We have a hiring freeze; who owns this internally without new headcount?
Walk me through the exit clauses and data egress fees if we leave in year two

rubric.label: Business case
rubric.what: Frames value in CFO language: net ARR impact, payback period, and risk-adjusted cash flow.

rubric.label: Financial modeling
rubric.what: Builds transparent, driver-based models the finance team can audit and adopt as their own.

rubric.label: Objection handling
rubric.what: Addresses each pushback with data or a concession that protects core value.

rubric.label: Stakeholder alignment
rubric.what: Maps the buying group, surfaces hidden vetoes, and equips champions with internal talking points.

rubric.label: Competitive positioning
rubric.what: Differentiates on total cost of ownership and switching risk, not feature lists.

rubric.label: Compliance truth
rubric.what: Represents security, data residency, and contractual terms accurately without oversell.

pitfalls: Quoting list price instead of modeling the prospect’s actual usage ramp.
Promising security certifications or data residency that are on the roadmap not in production.
Conceding discount depth without expanding term or adding expansion triggers.
